title: cross-region-canary-mismatch-safe-promotion-gate-fix
creator: Lena Zhou
description: During a staged model rollout spanning eu-west and us-east regions, the control plane recorded a canary state drift: the promotion decision computed in the primary region did not sync to the secondary region's route table. This caused ~12% of traffic to be routed to an older pinned model in us-east while eu-west moved forward. The mismatch triggered an automated rollback attempt in us-east that failed due to version-pinlock logic, creating a transient dual-serve state and elevated tail latency for several customer routes. This ticket captures the post-incident follow-ups, proposed fixes, and ownership for preventing cross-region canary divergence.
impact_summary: ~6 hours of degraded routing consistency for a subset of customers across two regions; increased 99th percentile latency by ~180ms on affected routes; three customer-facing incidents (support tickets) logged; no data exfiltration. Business impact assessed as medium; SLA not breached but risk of regression high without fixes.
timeline: 2026-03-09T02:10Z - Rollout initiated: canary 5% traffic eu-west, 0% us-east (scheduled staged promotion).

2026-03-09T02:42Z - Promotion evaluator in eu-west marked canary as 'pass' based on latency/quality thresholds. Promotion intent written to control plane but control-plane sync job to us-east failed intermittently (timeout + partial state).
2026-03-09T03:05Z - Observability alerts: cross-region route divergence detected by rollout-consistency monitor. SRE paged.
2026-03-09T03:12Z - Automated rollback attempted in us-east due to local healthcheck flapping; rollback could not complete because version-pinlock flag remained set from previous pinned deployment.
2026-03-09T04:00Z - Manual intervention: traffic manually rebalanced to safe fallback model; emergency runbook executed to clear pinlock and reconcile route states.
2026-03-09T07:30Z - Post-incident triage meeting; decision to open full postmortem and block similar cross-region promotions until mitigations in place.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a staged rollout with asymmetric promotion triggers across regions (simulate network partition of control-plane sync).
2) Force primary region evaluator to mark canary 'pass' while blocking control-plane replication to secondary region for >= 3 minutes.
3) Ensure secondary region still has an active version-pinlock set from previous operations so automated rollback cannot complete.
4) Observe mixed-serve state and increased tail latency on affected routes.
Notes: reproduction harness saved as a Jenkins job and linked in related_links.
root_cause: The control plane's cross-region state replication used a best-effort sync (no strong consistency guarantee). A recent optimization (async write-path introduced in runtime-1.18) reduced promotion latency but removed the verification step that ensured destination route tables applied the same promotion intent. Separately, version-pinlock semantics allowed stale locks to persist when partial rollbacks occurred, blocking automated reconciliation. The combination produced a window where regions diverged and rollback automation could not progress.
mitigating_actions_taken: Immediate: manually executed the emergency reconciliation runbook to clear pinlock and force consistent route state across regions.
Short-term: paused cross-region promotions and disabled async-only promotions until a consistency check is implemented.
Monitoring: added temporary dashboard and alert (rollout.consistency.delta) to detect region routing deltas >1%.
Customer comms: support team sent templated updates to affected customers and logged incident details in Status page.
proposed_action_items: A1: Implement a two-phase commit (2PC)-style promotion handshake for multi-region rollouts: write promotion intent, verify region acknowledgements, then flip traffic. Owner: Marco Rivera. Due: 2026-04-07.
A2: Add an atomic canary-state-consistency check in the control plane that rejects promotions when destination region state differs. Owner: Priya Natarajan. Due: 2026-03-31.

A3: Harden version-pinlock lifecycle: ensure pinlock TTLs and an orphaned-lock reconciler that can safely clear stale locks after operator approval or automated safety checks. Owner: SRE team (Jessica Kim). Due: 2026-04-14.

A4: Create a rollout-dry-run job that simulates promotion intent propagation across regions without flipping traffic; integrate into CI for every release. Owner: Platform QE (Diego Alvarez). Estimate: 3 points. Due: 2026-03-28.
A5: Expand rollout observability: add per-region expected-vs-applied route snapshot, and automated alerting for mismatch >0.5% for production. Owner: Observability (Hannah Li). Due: 2026-03-21.
A6: Update rollout runbook with explicit cross-region reconciliation steps, a pinlock recovery checklist, and post-reconciliation validation steps. Owner: Oncall runbook maintainers. Due: 2026-03-18.
A7: Add unit + integration tests for async-write promotion path covering partial failures and rollback scenarios. Owner: Runtime dev (Omar Farouk). Estimate: 5 points. Due: 2026-04-07.
A8: Schedule a tabletop incident exercise to rehearse cross-region promotion failures next on-call cycle. Owner: SRE lead. Due: 2026-04-01.
acceptance_criteria: All action items assigned and tracked in this ticket or child tickets.
Control plane implements acknowledgement-based promotion with automated tests verifying cross-region parity.
Pinlock reconciler in place and tested on a canary namespace; TTLs configured and documented.
New alerts and dashboard panels visible in the Console; no silent mismatches for 14 days of staged promotions in staging environment.
Runbook updated and tabletop exercise completed with post-exercise notes.
review_feedback: PM (Carlos Mendes): 'Need clearer rollout gating UX in Console so ops can block cross-region promotions from the UI until parity is confirmed.'
Design (Rina Kapoor): 'Suggest we add visual indicators in the rollout timeline and per-region diff view; we can prototype in Console-2026.03.'
SRE (Jessica Kim): 'Pinlock TTL must be conservative; propose default 2h TTL with automatic reconciliation on stale locks older than TTL.'
Runtime (Omar Farouk): '2PC adds latency; we should make it optional per-customer (configurable policy) but enabled by default for multi-region promotions.'
notes: This event surfaced a trade-off we accepted in runtime-1.18 to prioritize promotion latency. The mitigation plan balances operator UX, safety, and latency: make strong-consistency promotions the default for cross-region, provide an opt-out policy for single-region customers, and improve instrumentation. Next steps: break down A1/A2 into sub-tasks (control-plane API, state machine, integration tests) and schedule a sprint slot in Cycle 2026-W12.
